title: Scroll Snap and Scroll-Driven Animations
summary: Guide scrolling to useful positions and connect motion to scroll progress.

subtopics.title: Choose a scroll snapping container
subtopics.explanation: `scroll-snap-type` turns a scroll container into a snapping area and sets the axis and strictness. For example, `x mandatory` asks a horizontal carousel to stop at a snap point. Use `proximity` when a gentle alignment is enough, so users can still scroll freely through content.

subtopics.title: Set each item’s snap position
subtopics.explanation: `scroll-snap-align` marks where an item should line up inside its container. A card can use `start` so its leading edge meets the viewport edge after scrolling. Add `scroll-margin` when a sticky header would cover the snapped item, and test with keyboard and touch input.

subtopics.title: Connect animation progress to scrolling
subtopics.explanation: A scroll timeline maps animation progress to how far a user has scrolled, rather than to elapsed time. For example, a reading progress bar can fill as an article moves through the viewport. Keep the effect decorative, provide a reduced-motion alternative, and confirm browser support before relying on it.

subtopics.title: Respect reduced-motion preferences
subtopics.explanation: Some people disable nonessential motion because it causes discomfort or distraction. Use `prefers-reduced-motion` to remove or simplify scroll-linked movement for those users. The content and any progress information should remain understandable without animation; motion must not be the only way to communicate a change.

subtopics.title: Preserve scroll and keyboard control
subtopics.explanation: Snapping should guide scrolling without trapping the user at one item. Test wheel, touch, keyboard, and assistive-technology navigation, especially when the container has many cards. If a user cannot reach or leave an item naturally, loosen the snap behavior or remove it.

foundations.overview: Scroll snapping helps a scroll container settle on selected positions, such as cards in a carousel. Scroll-driven animations tie an animation timeline to scroll position. These features can improve browsing, but must not trap users or make content hard to reach.
foundations.mentalModel: It is like a book that naturally opens to marked sections.
foundations.whyItMatters: They let a page respond to how far someone has moved through content.

keyTakeaways: Scroll timelines connect animation progress to scrolling.
Keep free scrolling and keyboard access usable.
